doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Rutgers and the Institute of Jazz Studies
title: Donations of 78s and LPs to the Institute
summary: People constantly offer record collections the Institute has no space for.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I love reading about those guys. Like in Bill Crow’s book, you know.

It’s the jazz life. And sometimes you wonder – well that’s another subject, about then and now. I cracked up at the rehearsal, I think it was last night, because one guy was going to say, he was saying, “we’re going to take a donation to collect a little money for some of the ringers.” So he says, “we’re taking a donation” and someone said, “do you take 78s?” I said, “How perfect is that?” What to do with the 78s.
Oh God we get that almost every day. So, but it’s, “Oh my father just died,” or, you know, “he had a collection of 78s.” Mostly it’s LPs that they want to give us. And you

know, and they’re so convinced these are the most greatest most unique collection in the world, and, “Oh it’s got lots of Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington and Count Basie.” And I hate to always tell them, “Yeah, these are probably kind of common LPs. We probably have every one of them that he had in his collection too, and we just can’t take them because we have no space.” The space is not there.
